transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-05
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Liam (CSM) / Sofia (Peregrine ML Ops), Ethan (CTO), Priya (InfoSec), Marco (SRE)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um this is Maya from Redwood, joining today with Daniel and Liam. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Sofia: good thanks, busy sprint week but all good.
[00:11] Ethan: hey all, quick note I'm at a lunch meeting but will be on and off, priya will cover security bits.
[00:17] Maya: cool, we'll try to keep it tight. agenda is renewal + adding eu region and a short apac burst plan, plus any security follow-ups. is that right Sofia?
[00:27] Sofia: yep that's it. main ask is: can we get EU region live before June and a short burst capacity for APAC for our campaign end of May. also want to finalize contract term.
[00:36] Daniel: great — from the technical side we'll want to validate your traffic pattern. do you have the 7-day p95 and p99 latency and top endpoints?
[00:44] Sofia: i pulled a summary — we'll share the CSV, but rough p95 token latencies are around 180-220ms on average for text-gen calls, p99 spikes to 520ms when KV cache warms.
[00:56] Marco: and the traffic shape is pretty spiky, especially at 09:00 and 19:00 UTC where we see 3x baseline — that is why the burst ask.
[01:06] Daniel: okay that's useful. if we configure Dedicated reserved capacity for EU plus a burst policy for APAC, we can keep p95 under 200ms in steady state. p99 will depend on KV cache hit rate and prompt lengths.
[01:20] Priya: on encryption and keys — still need to confirm whether Redwood's KMS integration supports our HSM vendor. previously i saw a note about KMS integrations in the doc but vendor wasn't listed.
[01:30] Liam: noted, we'll include KMS vendor compatibility matrix. we support customer-managed keys via our KMS connector; sometimes naming shows up as, uh, the 'private key store' in older docs — we'll clarify.
[01:41] Ethan: timeline wise, our procurement wants contract signed by April 23 to hit June go-live. is that feasible if we start a small pilot now?
[01:50] Maya: yes, that's tight but doable. typical path is: sign renewal + region addendum, kick off provisioning for EU staging, run a verification benchmark, then flip DNS/ingress for production. provisioning for EU staging usually 7-10 business days.
[02:05] Sofia: so if we sign by 4/23, provisioning could start same week and staging up by early May. good.
[02:12] Daniel: i'd like to propose a 2-phase verification: 1) functional smoke + load at steady qps, 2) KV-warm stress for p99. we'll run a small 1hr test with your SREs.
[02:24] Marco: 1hr test is fine. can you provide the test runner script? we prefer reproducible scripts not just a runbook.
[02:31] Daniel: yes we'll share a bench script — it's the same harness we use for Dedicated sizing. i'll send a sanitized version.
[02:37] Maya: quick commercial note — for EU region add-on we can either do a flat monthly for reserved nodes or a committed monthly token minimum; given your spikiness i'd recommend reserved + burst buffer. we'll model both in the quote.
[02:51] Sofia: pricing transparency is important — last time we had surprise tokens from repeated retries. can we get a token breakdown by endpoint?
[02:59] Liam: yep, we'll include per-route token estimates and historical token usage bands. we'll also call out retries and sync behavior — sometimes transient 5xx cause retries and token double-counts.
[03:13] Priya: also need audit logs and retention policy documented for SOC2. we want 12 months of immutable logs for inference requests and admin actions. can Redwood provide that?
[03:23] Maya: we provide audit logs and can extend retention as an add-on. i will attach the exact retention SLA and format — note that request bodies may be redacted by default unless a contract clause allows capture of request payloads for troubleshooting.
[03:36] Priya: ok we will review but need clarification on redaction and access controls. SSO/SAML is a must and RBAC for team roles.
[03:44] Daniel: SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning are both supported. RBAC can be scoped to route-level permissions. i'll capture the exact role names in the doc.
[03:52] Sofia: on latency — you mentioned cache strategy. our prompts for claims summarization are usually long (avg 1,200 tokens) and we see more p99 variance with longer contexts. does Redwood Dedicated handle long K-V cache efficiently?
[04:04] Daniel: yes, the runtime is optimized for large KV windows; we have quantization-friendly paths and continuous batching that help. that said, long context length increases memory pressure; we might recommend a slightly bigger instance SKU for EU reserved pool. we'll include that in the technical notes.
[04:20] Ethan: any suggestions on prompt engineering to reduce per-call cost without losing quality? we've been experimenting with truncation and structured output.
[04:28] Daniel: a couple of levers — structured function outputs to reduce tokens, prefix caching for shared system prompts, and token-level caching for repeated candidate retrieval. we'll include recommended config changes.
[04:39] Maya: moving to blockers — what would prevent you from signing? timeline? security? price?
[04:45] Sofia: principal blockers are 1) procurement wants the final legal language for data residency, 2) InfoSec needs KMS/HSM confirmation, 3) we want to see one verification run with p99 under 800ms for long prompts.
[04:58] Priya: and we need an exact list of compliance artifacts — AICPA, network diagrams, SOC2 Type II cert copy.
[05:06] Liam: we'll attach SOC2 Type II, network diagram, a sample of our audit log export, and the KMS integration matrix.
[05:12] Maya: ask for timeline check — we'll send the quote by 2026-04-09, docs the same day, and schedule the verification for 2026-04-14. does that sound good?
[05:20] Ethan: yes, that aligns with procurement.
[05:23] Sofia: can we also get a simple demo of the rollout and fallback behavior — e.g., if EU capacity saturated, how does traffic fail to hosted or another region? we want a clear SLA of fallback.
[05:33] Daniel: absolutely. our routing policies support region-based failover and model variants. we'll demo a canary and automatic fallback policy in the verification session. note: fallback to hosted may change latency characteristics.
[05:45] Marco: one more ops question: during bursts will you throttle at the gateway or queue? how are tokens accounted if requests are queued for 60s?
[05:55] Daniel: we have burst buckets and request queuing; tokens are charged on execution, not queue time. however retries that re-send the same request will incur additional tokens. we'll propose a timeout and circuit-breaker config.
[06:08] Priya: any third-party vendor risks? procurement asked about subcontractors and if data leaves EU during processing.
[06:15] Maya: for EU region option we keep processing within the EU region cluster; we will detail our subprocessors and data flow in the DPA addendum.
[06:24] Sofia: ok great. i also want to confirm whether we can do private deployment (VPC) later after initial go-live. that's part of roadmap.
[06:31] Maya: yes private deployment is supported — we can add that as a staged milestone in the contract. provisioning timeline is longer (4–6 weeks) and includes network setup and KMS exchange.
[06:41] Ethan: let's be explicit about costs and timeline in the quote, otherwise procurement will push back.
[06:46] Maya: understood. we'll include a cost and timeline table.
[06:50] (silence ~15s)
[07:05] Maya: okay last thing — competitors. are you running any parallel evals?
[07:10] Sofia: we're doing a light parallel proof of concept with a self-hosted stack for compliance reasons. also had a short eval with Anthropic for some completion quality tests.
[07:20] Liam: good to know. we'll make sure to highlight where our serving runtime reduces p99 and cost compared to a pure self-hosted approach.
[07:27] Maya: recap of next steps — we'll send renewal quote with region addendum by 4/9, include SOC2 and KMS matrix, Daniel will send bench script by 4/8, schedule verify session 4/14. action owners on the recording.
[07:41] Sofia: thanks everyone. one last tiny ask — can we get a one-page TLDR that procurement can read?
[07:47] Maya: yes, we'll include a TL;DR one-pager with costs, timeline, and key compliance bullets.
[07:53] Ethan: thanks.
[07:55] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

(End of recording)
